For the specified lower-bit signing the coordinate flips anticommute and square to the identity, so A²=4I and |S|≤16; S is divisible by four (the all-plus score is 8, and flips preserve the score modulo four). The sign-pattern ratio of two negative-plaquette signings has trivial holonomy because cube cycles are generated by squares, proving gauge equivalence. Independent exact reproduction conditioned on the eight even vertices. For fixed even spins a, the eight odd spins contribute the product of (z^h+z^(−h)) over their signed fields h, computed by integer convolution; this counts all 256 times 256 choices, including zero fields with factor 2. The resulting ordered score counts are [16,1920,8640,13440,17504,13440,8640,1920,16], totaling 65536, with second and fourth moments 32 and 2432. If k fields have size 4 there are 8−4k of size 2, so k=0,1,2. Exactly one sign completion reaches score +16 for each k=0 assignment. Each of the eight fields has size 4 for precisely 32 of the 256 even-spin choices, hence mean k=1. With independently confirmed 16 choices at k=0 this gives class counts (16,224,16). The three distinct conditional spin polynomials then give the full nonextremal histogram.

value.rationale: The four-cube is a natural finite cell studied for its unusually simple frustrated ground configurations and orthogonal interaction matrix, not an arbitrary truncation chosen after enumeration. The complete entropy by energy level provides exact excited-state weights and a reproducible finite-temperature benchmark for that standard instance. A ground energy, extremal signing/field histogram or limiting free energy alone omits those multiplicities. This is a limited finite invariant, not a thermodynamic-limit claim.
